{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that the relationship between insecurity and election fraud follows an inverted U-shape, where fraud increases with violence up to a certain level and then decreases.",
  "design": "correlational",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Insurgent violence (measured as the number of attacks per 1,000 population in a two-month window before the election).",
  "outcome_measure": "Election fraud (measured at the district level using a last-digit forensic test on polling station vote counts).",
  "population_and_setting": "398 districts in Afghanistan during the 2009 presidential election.",
  "sample_size_total": 375,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Not applicable (observational study using administrative election data).",
  "analysis_plan": "Logit regression of the binary fraud indicator on violence and its squared term, controlling for the number of closed polling stations, electrification, per-capita expenditure, distance from Kabul, and elevation.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "The study uses geocoded military reports (SIGACT) for violence data and polling-station level election returns. The fraud measure is validated against physical inspection data from a national ballot recount."
}
